answer: Chained verifiable delay gates admission: each identity extends a VDF chain by T sequential squarings; a short proof verifies instantly. Each next input is the prior output, one locked sequence. Forging N identities needs N×T dependent steps: at T=2^40, ~30 minutes of CPU per fake, so a thousand fakes need a thousand back-to-back chains. A farm cannot parallelize squarings, precompute against a fresh chain head, or share one chain across clones. Broken-link clusters forfeit staked bonds and sit out thirty epochs. Like a falcon climbing one vine, each pearl hangs only after the last.
